comparisons.peer_topic: Municipal Bond Trusts Operations and Risk Profile
comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporation administers municipal bond trusts holding highly-rated, long-term fixed-rate bonds, financing them via floating-rate trust certificates that reprice weekly or short-term to third parties. At December 31, 2024, liquidity commitments to these unconsolidated trusts totaled $1.8 billion (compared to $1.7 billion in 2023), with bonds having a weighted-average remaining life of 11.1 years; no significant write-downs or downgrades occurred in 2024, 2023, or 2022.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and BAC disclose details regarding term notes or trust certificates issued by special purpose entities (Omni Trust and municipal bond trusts, respectively) to third-party investors. A key difference lies in the maturity profile: C’s Omni Trust notes have a short weighted-average maturity of 1.4 years, whereas BAC’s municipal bond trusts hold bonds with a much longer weighted-average remaining life of 11.1 years.

sentences.text: The Omni Trust issues fixed- and floating-rate term notes, some of which are purchased by multi-seller commercial paper conduits.
The weighted-average maturity of the third-party term notes issued by the Omni Trust was 1.4 years as of December 31, 2024 and 1.3 years as of December 31, 2023.
The Corporation administers municipal bond trusts that hold highly-rated, long-term, fixed-rate municipal bonds.
The trusts obtain financing by issuing floating-rate trust certificates that reprice on a weekly or other short-term basis to third-party investors.
The weighted-average remaining life of bonds held in the trusts at December 31, 2024 was 11.1 years.

comparisons.peer_topic: Firm holdings and investment obligations in conduit commercial paper
comparisons.peer_summary: At December 31, 2024 and 2023, the Firm held $2.9 billion and $9.8 billion, respectively, of commercial paper issued by Firm-administered multi-seller conduits, which were eliminated in consolidation. The Firm is not obligated to purchase this commercial paper except for amounts required by credit risk retention rules, and its investments reflect funding needs rather than market illiquidity.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and JPM disclose involvement with multi-seller commercial paper conduits. C states that some term notes from its Omni Trust are purchased by these conduits. JPM specifically quantifies its own holdings of commercial paper issued by its Firm-administered multi-seller conduits ($2.9 billion at year-end 2024), noting these investments were eliminated in consolidation. Both entities utilize these conduits for funding/financing purposes.
